topic: Carrying kids and bags on one side

slides.headline: Always carry on the same side?
slides.sub: Kids, bags and shopping: small swaps that spread the load.

slides.title: One-sided carrying is normal
slides.body: Most of us have a favourite hip for a toddler and a favourite shoulder for a bag. It's not harmful, but doing it for hours every day can leave one side feeling tired and achy.

slides.title: Swap sides on purpose
slides.body: Try switching hips or shoulders at each doorway, or every few minutes on a walk. It feels awkward at first, but giving your usual side a break often makes a noticeable difference.

slides.title: Change the carry, not just the side
slides.body: Front carriers, backpacks with both straps on and shopping split into two even bags all spread the load. Hold kids close to your body rather than perched out on one hip.

slides.title: Build strength for the job
slides.body: Carrying is a lifting task, so train it. Farmer's carries, suitcase carries with a bag in one hand, squats and rows a couple of times a week can help your body handle daily loads.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: Get checked if pain spreads down an arm or leg with numbness or weakness, keeps waking you at night, or isn't easing after a few weeks despite changes to how you carry.

slides.headline: Sore from the daily carry?
slides.body: Book with our chiropractors at Hybrid Physiotherapy. We'll assess your back, neck and shoulders, use hands-on care where it helps and give you exercises for daily lifting.

caption:
Toddler always on the left hip? Bag always on the right shoulder?

One-sided carrying is normal and not harmful, but hours of it every day can leave one side feeling tired and achy. Swap sides on purpose, like at every doorway. Use both backpack straps, split shopping into two even bags, and hold kids close to your body rather than perched out on a hip.

Carrying is lifting, so train for it: farmer's carries, suitcase carries, squats and rows a couple of times a week help your body handle the daily load.

Get checked if pain spreads down an arm or leg with numbness or weakness, or keeps waking you at night.
